title: I made a mobile game where your weapon is an ancient musical instrument and you generate the BGM as you fight
author: WuxiaScrub
selftext:
**Game Title:** Jianghu: Sword & Zither

**Google Play:** [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hdexpanse.qinjianjianghu](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hdexpanse.qinjianjianghu)  
  
**iOS:** [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/jianghu-sword-zither/id6800447224](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/jianghu-sword-zither/id6800447224)

**Description:** In this Wuxia-themed roguelite, you wield an ancient Chinese instrument as your weapon and defeat waves of incoming enemies using combinations of gestures inspired by how the real instrument is played, with each stroking pattern mapping to a different type of attack. What's unique about this game is that there is no fixed background music. You generate the music as you fight.

There's a boss every 10 waves, each with their own unique strengths and mechanics. As you level up your character, you can use cultivation points for permanent stat upgrades or unlock powerful assists. Compete in global/monthly/weekly high scores and earn permanent trophy counts for being in the top 3 each month!

comments.author: joshbuildsstuff
comments.body: Did you do the music yourself?  The only thing that bothers me about the trailer is it seems like nothing syncs up with the actual gameplay even though the whole unique thing about this game is there is no fixed background music.

replies.author: WuxiaScrub
replies.body: That's just the trailer music, but in-game music is different. I have another longer video that shows a clip of actual gameplay, but for the trailer, I put a bgm over it.

replies.author: Unlikely_Perspective
replies.body: Just my opinion but I would prefer to hear what it sounds like, I unmuted to hear what the game sounds like but was disappointed.

replies.author: WuxiaScrub
replies.body: I see, thanks for sharing your thoughts! Here's the longer video: [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/hLKUbak2HgU](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/hLKUbak2HgU) Around 50 second mark is in-game sound. :)
